1 Vehicles Act, 1988 filed by the petitioner Deputy Commissioner of Police, Police Control Room (PCR) Delhi with respect to damage caused to government gypsy which was a PCR vehicle in an accident caused by respondent no. 1 Shahnawaj with his car.
2. The inquiry proceeded and the petitioner has led evidence in this case.

sentences.text: The total compensation claimed in the petition is Rs.29,864/- which was the bill incurred for the repair of the PCR van through the invoice Ex.PW4/1.
Initially, the case reached final arguments after closing the opportunity of respondent to lead evidence.
However, the respondent's application for leading evidence was allowed on 12.10.2021 after which the respondents had not led any evidence for last two-three dates.

There were efforts to settle the issue and on last date the parokar of the petitioner was directed to appear in person to clarify the offer of the insurance company that it was willing to pay the claimed amount.
However, today there was no definite answer from the side of the petitioner.
ASI Sanjeev Kumar present in the Court states that he has no instructions and for long time there is no parokar in this case.
The case is pending since 2016.

I think since the respondent no.3/insurance company is ready to pay the bill of repairs of the PCR van for which this claim was filed, there is no need to stretch the matter further and it is better that this cause come to an end.
Separate statement of counsel for respondent no. 3/insurance company was recorded.

In view of the same, an Award of Rs.29,864/- (Rs. Twenty-Nine Thousand Eight Hundred & Sixty-Four only) as claimed by the petitioner in his petition in favour of petitioner against the respondent no.3,
insurance company is passed.
This award is required to be deposited in the form of demand draft/cheque or transfer through NEFT/RTGS by the insurance company in favour of PO MACT East Delhi within 30 days.
